name: Rafik Al-Hariri
profile: Former Prime Minister of Lebanon and construction billionaire (Saudi Oger). Assassinated by a truck bomb in Beirut on 14 February 2005.

name: Denis Defforey
profile: Co-founder of French hypermarket chain Carrefour (1959) and its CEO 1985-1990. Died 6 February 2006 aged 80.
notes: Deceased (d. 6 Feb 2006). Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denis_Defforey (cites Le Monde obituary, 14 Feb 2006).

name: David Hamilton Koch
profile: Co-owner and former executive vice president of Koch Industries, major philanthropist and political donor. Died 23 August 2019 aged 79.

name: Akira Mori
current_role: Chairman, Mori Trust Co., Ltd. and Mori Trust Holdings (reconfirmed in June 24, 2026 officer list)
profile: Born 1936 in Kyoto, son of Mori Building founder Taikichiro Mori. He split the family business with brother Minoru in 1999 and built Mori Trust into an owner of 100+ office buildings and hotels across Japan. Since 2016 his daughter Miwako Date is president/CEO, expanding overseas (e.g. ~50% of a Park Avenue tower for ~$700M in 2023).
interesting_fact: Mori Trust bought close to a 50% stake in a 45-story Park Avenue office tower in New York for about $700 million in 2023, part of a push to put ~20% of new investment overseas.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family real-estate business, he graduated from Keio University in 1960 and started his career at Yasuda Trust & Banking (now part of Mizuho Trust & Banking); he only formally joined Mori Building as an employee in 1972.
notes: Age ~90; day-to-day leadership is with daughter Miwako Date (President & CEO), who is the more realistic interview target. Mori Trust press releases go out via digitalpr.jp. Officer list: https://www.mori-trust.co.jp/assets/media/20260624_1.pdf

name: Ji Qi
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, H World Group (Nasdaq: HTHT; HKEX: 1179)
profile: Shanghai Jiao Tong University-educated serial entrepreneur who co-founded Ctrip (now Trip.com) in 1999 and Home Inns in 2002, then founded HanTing/China Lodging in 2005, now H World Group, which runs 13,000+ mostly budget and midscale hotels (Hi Inn, Ji Hotel, and others). He remains executive chairman; CEO Hui Jin runs day-to-day operations.
interesting_fact: Often described as the first Chinese entrepreneur to found three companies that each passed a $1B valuation and listed on Nasdaq: Ctrip/Trip.com, Home Inns and H World (formerly China Lodging/Huazhu).
deep_cut_fact: He wrote 'The Founder's Notes' (LID Publishing, 2020), a book of essays on applying Chinese philosophy and the pursuit of 'Truth, Goodness and Beauty' to company culture and management.
notes: Listed as Singapore resident. Company IR is the main published route; his book publisher (LID Publishing) is a possible secondary angle.

name: Liu Yiqian
current_role: Chairman, Sunline Group (Shanghai investment company); co-founder, Long Museum
profile: Shanghai-born (1963) former taxi driver who made his fortune from the mid-1980s trading early Chinese stocks (including buying pre-IPO employee shares in state firms), real estate and pharmaceuticals, run through Sunline Group. With wife Wang Wei he founded the Long Museum (Shanghai Pudong 2012, West Bund 2014, Chongqing), one of China's biggest private museums.
interesting_fact: In 2015 he bought Modigliani's 'Nu couche' for $170.4 million, reportedly paying with an American Express Centurion card; a year earlier he paid ~$36M for a Ming 'chicken cup'.
deep_cut_fact: He left school at 14 to help his mother sell handbags on the street, and met his wife and museum co-founder Wang Wei while working as a Shanghai taxi driver in the mid-1980s. In 2004 he also founded Tianping Auto Insurance and Guohua Life Insurance.
notes: Press email is from a 2014 Long Museum press release; verify still active. The Wire China reports he declined interview requests recently; low-profile. Wife Wang Wei is the museum's public face.

name: Sam Altman
profile: Stanford dropout who founded Loopt (sold 2012 for $43M), ran Y Combinator as president 2014-2019, then became OpenAI CEO (briefly fired and rehired in 2023). He holds no OpenAI equity; his wealth comes from investments such as Stripe, Reddit and fusion company Helion. He stepped down as Oklo chair in April 2025 and as Helion chair in March 2026, citing AI-energy partnerships.
interesting_fact: In 2021 he put $375 million into fusion startup Helion Energy, his largest startup investment at the time; he had chaired Oklo (advanced fission) since 2015 and took it public via his SPAC, which makes him central to the AI-power story.
deep_cut_fact: He got his first computer, an Apple Macintosh, at age eight and learned to code and take its hardware apart.
notes: Extremely high-demand guest. Oklo stepdown: https://www.neimagazine.com/news/sam-altman-steps-down-as-oklo-chair/ ; Helion stake was scrutinised in the 2026 Musk v. OpenAI trial (https://www.geekwire.com/2026/openai-ceo-sam-altmans-stake-in-helion-energy-draws-scrutiny-in-musk-trial-and-on-capitol-hill/). No OpenAI press email is published first-party (third-party sites list press@openai.com, unverified). Best route is OpenAI comms or a warm intro.
